annotations.title: Pay transparency obligations in Poland (jawność wynagrodzeń)

description: Use for pay transparency in Poland (jawność wynagrodzeń): pay ranges for candidates, the right to pay information, gender pay gap reports by company size and the status of Directive 2023/970. Give the legal basis and the verification date of each fact. Pay transparency in Poland with dates and the state today: since 24 December 2025 every employer gives job candidates the starting pay or pay range (in the job ad, before the interview or before the contract), keeps job ads and titles gender-neutral and may not ask about current or previous pay (Labour Code art. 18^3ca, 22^1). EU Directive 2023/970 (deadline 7 June 2026) adds access to pay criteria, the right to request pay information, the end of pay secrecy clauses, gender pay gap reports (250+ employees every year and 150-249 every 3 years from 7 June 2027; 100-149 every 3 years from 7 June 2031) and a joint pay assessment at a 5% unexplained gap. Each obligation says whether a Polish act already applies it or it waits for the Polish implementing bill (government draft UC127, status and check date included). Pass employees to get only the obligations for a company of that size.
